cards.text: Next, Jesus and His disciples come to Jericho, and now they're heading out of town with a large crowd. Sitting beside the road is a blind beggar named Bartimaeus, the son of Timaeus. He can't see a thing, but he can hear the whole crowd coming his way.

cards.question: Bartimaeus hears that it's Jesus of Nazareth passing by. He can't see Him or walk over to Him. What does he do?

answers.text: He starts crying out to Jesus
He sends someone to bring Jesus
He waits for the crowd to pass

cards.text: He shouts, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!” He can't see where Jesus is, so he's making DOUBLE sure Jesus can hear where HE is.

cards.question: A blind beggar is shouting in the middle of a big crowd. Many of the people tell Bartimaeus to be ___.

cards.text: Many people tell him to be silent. I bet he got THE look, the one a whole room gives you when your phone goes off in a quiet meeting and your ringtone is a trumpet solo.

cards.question: When the crowd tells Bartimaeus to be silent, he quiets down and waits.

cards.text: He cries out all the LOUDER: “Son of David, have mercy on me!” They told this man to hush, and he heard TURN IT UP.

cards.question: Jesus is leaving Jericho with a large crowd, and one voice keeps shouting for mercy. What does Jesus do?

answers.text: He stops and has him called over
He keeps walking and waves to him
He sends a disciple to bless him

cards.text: Jesus stops and says, “Call him.” So they call the blind man.

cards.question: Somebody finally has good news for Bartimaeus. What do they tell him?

answers.text: Take courage because Jesus is calling him
Stay put because Jesus will come by later
Go home because Jesus has no time today

cards.question: When Bartimaeus hears that Jesus is calling for him, he jumps up and comes to Jesus.

cards.text: He even throws off his cloak to get there. Friend, I have hit SNOOZE on days I was excited about, and this man is out of his cloak before anybody finishes saying “Get up!”
Jesus asks him, “What do you want Me to do for you?” That's the exact question He just asked James and John, and they asked to sit at His right and left in His glory (Mark 10:36-37).

cards.question: Bartimaeus calls Jesus “Rabboni” and asks Him to let him ___ again.

cards.text: No seats, no glory, just his eyes. Jesus tells him, “Go, your faith has healed you.”

cards.question: After Jesus tells him his faith has healed him, Bartimaeus has to wait a while for his sight to come back.
Bartimaeus can see, and Jesus just told him “Go.” Where does he go?

answers.text: He follows Jesus along the road
He goes home to his family

cards.text: Immediately he can see, and he follows Jesus along the road. The man who started out sitting beside the road ends up on it, following Jesus.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 15 quotes "Go, your faith has healed you.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question says Bartimaeus can't walk over to Jesus. The text never says that, and Mark 10:50 shows him jumping up and coming to Jesus.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: "He can't see where Jesus is, so he's making DOUBLE sure Jesus can hear where HE is" gives a reason for his shouting as fact. Mark 10:47 doesn't say why he cries out.

rule.text: Reasons: He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The question puts Bartimaeus "in the middle of a big crowd." Mark 10:46 says he was sitting beside the road as the crowd left Jericho.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The card's only passage content is the answer to card 4 (many people tell him to be silent), followed by a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The setup line "Somebody finally has good news for Bartimaeus" rules out the wrong answers "Go home because Jesus has no time today" and "Stay put because Jesus will come by later."

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card quotes "Get up!" from Mark 10:49 but cites only Mark 10:50.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: James and John show up for the first time in this lesson without saying who they are, such as two of Jesus' disciples.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This is a where question, but the wrong answer "He goes home to his family" isn't a real detail from somewhere in the Bible.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.
